limitations: Poppler is an independent extractor, not OCR ground truth.
PDFium with both Hebrew flags off can still infer spacing; this does not identify PDF object bytes.
The query retains whitespace and only permits Hebrew marks between letters.

proof.scope: PDFium extraction including inferred spacing; not raw PDF object bytes

conclusions.dominantMeasuredComponent: Worker raw-build: PDFium calls plus Dart string/rectangle construction; the observations do not separate native extraction from this Dart construction.
conclusions.normalization: Hebrew normalization accounts for about one tenth of the instrumented caller interval. Two reference pages have unchanged text/geometry when both Hebrew flags are off; this does not establish that normalization is redundant for other pages or encodings.
conclusions.residual: Queue/dispatch/arena/return plus instrumentation bookkeeping remain combined in the outside-worker residual. It is not an isolated transfer measurement or a concurrent-queue measurement.
conclusions.overhead: The uninstrumented controls and instrumented callers are close in these ABBA observations. A small or negative observed difference is not evidence of product acceleration or exact zero observer overhead.
conclusions.productAction: Prioritize avoiding repeated raw extraction or optimizing the upstream raw-text construction contract. The existing app LRU thrash evidence remains relevant; these source-instrumented diagnostics are not an app optimization.
conclusions.reference: MG page 10 has 3,954 Hebrew letters and 378 marks in every extractor. Literal אלהים has zero hits; the marks-tolerant query has one hit (אֶלְהִים) in PDFium with flags both on/off and in Poppler layout, but none in Poppler raw. Extraction order/spacing differs, and OCR accuracy has no ground truth here.

limitations: Worker raw-build includes PDFium calls and Dart text/rectangle construction.
The outside-worker residual includes queue, dispatch, arena management, return and instrumentation bookkeeping; it is not isolated transfer time.
Worker counters are read/reset through a separate job outside each timed page interval.
Serial page calls do not measure a concurrent render/search backlog.
Instrumented durations include observer overhead and are not a product speedup.
No native-allocation, Dart-allocation, UI-latency or cold OS-cache claim.
Two independent processes per variant; repeated passes are not independent processes.
Hashes are computed between timed loads and can affect later GC or caches in both variants.
Instrumentation adds clocks and metric bookkeeping; the control is an overhead reference, not a product baseline/candidate.
Each document uses its own CI job/host; cross-document timings are not paired product effects.
Only two processes per variant; six measured passes per side are not six independent launches.
Per-page proof hashes cover all text/geometry, but the artifact does not preserve every page's full coordinate array for independent re-extraction.
The flag-off comparison covers only one content page per document; it cannot justify disabling Hebrew normalization globally.
